title: Stopping the nearest loop

curriculum.title: Stopping the nearest loop with break
curriculum.answer:
## Stopping a scan with `break`

A `for` loop normally visits every item in a list, one after another. Sometimes you want to stop early, as soon as you find what you were looking for. That early stop is what `break` does: it exits the nearest loop immediately.

The usual pattern is scan plus test: loop over the list, use `if` to test each value, and call `break` only when the test is true. Code after the loop then continues normally.

```python
nums = [4, 7, 2, 9]
for n in nums:
    if n == 2:
        print("found two")
        break
    print(n)
```

```text
4
7
found two
```

Here `nums` is defined before the loop. The loop prints `4`, then `7`. When `n` becomes `2`, it prints `"found two"` and `break` stops the loop, so `9` is never visited.

`break` belongs to the loop, not just to the `if`. It runs only when its `if` branch runs:

```python
values = [6, 1, 2]
for v in values:
    if v > 5:
        print("big")
        break
    print(v)
```

```text
big
```

Only `6` makes `v > 5` true, so the loop stops immediately and prints `"big"`. With `break` removed, the first pass would also print `6`. Later passes would print `1` and `2`. The complete output would be `big`, `6`, `1`, `2`, each on its own line.

Common mistakes are putting `break` outside the `if`, so the loop always stops after the first item, or replacing `break` with another `print`, which does not stop anything. Checked attempts are not proof of durable mastery, so keep practicing short scans with `for`, `if`, and `break`.

exercise.title: First value above limit
exercise.instructions: Scan items from first to last. Assign found to the first value greater than limit and stop the scan. If no value is greater than limit, found stays 0. For example, items [3, 8, 9] with limit 5 gives found 8. Use for, if, and break. Do not reset items or limit.

fresh_exercise.title: First cold snap
fresh_exercise.instructions: Scan temps from first to last. Assign chilly to the first temperature less than cold and stop the scan. If no temperature is less than cold, chilly stays 0. For example, temps [4, -2, -5] with cold 0 gives chilly -2. Use for, if, and break. Do not reset temps or cold.
